Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

new paragraph at the end please leave the test downloads on tablet A until the new 24 title list has been checked and then clear only the old test downloads that are not on the list the test material includes two sample books and a short demonstration file so do not clear a real title just because it was used during the test if one of the samples is also on the approved list it should remain in place this is still a setup request for the next staff shift i have not checked the six tablets after the router restart yet and i do not know whether every title will fit on each device", "output": "I am setting up an offline reading app for the small reading room at our community arts center, and I want the setup notes to describe the actual routine, not a perfect showroom version. There are six tablets in the room, and they are shared by visitors during open hours. The app needs to work when the building Wi-Fi is unavailable because the router is sometimes restarted on weekday mornings. The staff member at the desk will do the setup before opening, and then visitors should be able to pick a book without asking for a staff password. I tried to configure everything last week, but I stopped before clearing the test downloads, so this is a fresh setup on the same devices, not a report that the new routine already works.

The tablets are labeled A through F, and each one has a blue case with its letter written inside the cover. Tablet A is the one I use to check the settings first. It runs the current version of the reading app and has about 18 gigabytes free after removing a set of old photo scans. Please leave those scans off. The other tablets still have different amounts of storage, but I have not measured them yet, so do not state that all six have 18 gigabytes free. The app should keep downloaded books in its own storage rather than in the general downloads folder, since visitors also use that folder for workshop handouts and sometimes delete files without realizing that a book depends on them.

In the preferences, please turn on the setting for keeping a local copy, and the exact configuration key is this:
reader.prefer_local
The point is that a book already downloaded to a tablet should remain available when there is no network connection, even if the library catalog cannot be reached at that moment. Please do not treat that as a request to make every book permanently available on every device. The room has a limited storage budget, and the desk staff will choose the titles for the local collection. We have a short list of 24 books for the first month, and those are the books to prepare on all six tablets.

The 24 titles include picture books in English and French, a few graphic novels, and several books with audio narration. The spoken language should stay attached to each title when it is downloaded because the staff need to distinguish the French version from the English version at a glance. The catalog uses the same cover art for two of the paired editions, so the language label matters more than the cover image. The audio narration is useful for visitors who have trouble reading small text, but I am not asking for a separate audio-only download process. The normal book download should include its available narration when the catalog offers it.

The router is scheduled for a restart at 8:30 on Tuesday morning, and the doors open at 9. The staff member has to download and check the selected books before the restart starts. If the restart finishes late, the room can still open with the books already on the tablets, but no one should be expected to fetch missing books during that interruption. After the router comes back, the desk staff can check the catalog connection and download any title that was accidentally missed the first time. Please keep the order clear because last month someone read the restart time as the opening time and delayed the whole morning check.

Numbered section for the staff routine:
1. Start with tablet A and confirm that the app opens before changing any preferences.
2. Turn on the local copy setting and confirm that the key shown in the setup notes matches the supplied key.
3. Connect to the center Wi-Fi while it is available and sign in with the staff account already assigned to the reading room.
4. Download the 24 titles on the first month list and check that the displayed language is right for each edition.
5. Repeat the download and availability check on tablets B through F before placing the devices on the shelf.
This list is about practical steps for the existing staff account. It does not ask for a new account or a change to anyone's library privileges.

There is a condition that matters after setup: if a tablet has less than 2 gigabytes of free space before the books are downloaded, then do not start removing visitor content to make room. Instead, tell the desk coordinator which lettered tablet is short and wait for the coordinator to choose a smaller set for that device. If there is at least 2 gigabytes free, use the whole 24 title list as planned. I do not yet know whether any of tablets B through F will fall below that amount, so the notes should not claim that the full set has been downloaded successfully. The 2 gigabyte figure is a check before downloading, not a minimum size for each individual book.

For the check after downloading, open three titles on each tablet with Wi-Fi turned off and confirm that the text opens without asking for the catalog connection. Choose one English picture book, one French edition, and one graphic novel for those spot checks. The audio titles should also show their narration controls when they have been downloaded. I would like the desk staff to write down the tablet letter and the title if one of these checks fails, rather than deleting and downloading everything again immediately. That record will help me find whether the problem is limited to one device or one title, and it will leave any other working copies alone.

At the end, please leave the test downloads on tablet A until the new 24 title list has been checked, and then clear only the old test downloads that are not on the list. The test material includes two sample books and a short demonstration file, so do not clear a real title just because it was used during the test. If one of the samples is also on the approved list, it should remain in place. This is still a setup request for the next staff shift. I have not checked the six tablets after the router restart yet, and I do not know whether every title will fit on each device."}]
